recipe.purpose: Reproduce old-HEAD evidence without mutating the active checkout, Git index, or object database.
steps: Materialize sourceRevision with git archive into an isolated temporary source directory.
Build code-intel from that archive with cargo build -p code-intel --bin code-intel and an isolated target directory.
Create the deterministic fixture repository described below and commit it with the fixed identity, message, and timestamp.
Invoke the archived and current binaries with identical argv and repository inputs.
Record exact process exit code, stdout UTF-8 bytes, and stderr UTF-8 bytes; do not normalize any field.

fixtureRepository.content: src/lib.rs: pub fn fixture() {} followed by LF
fixtureRepository.purpose: Makes snapshot and repin success bytes deterministic without embedding a checkout path.

intentionalDeltas.name: full help alias discoverability
intentionalDeltas.reason: Phase 2 acceptance requires full help to expose every registered compatibility alias. The v1 bytes omitted aliases, so byte parity and alias completeness conflict; v2 resolves that conflict as one explicit versioned behavior change. Registering a route adds its line to these bytes (`serve --mcp`, #54): that is the same versioned behavior -- full help documents every registered route -- so the contract id pair stays v1 -> v2 rather than climbing a version per command.

intentionalDeltas.name: repin clean success
intentionalDeltas.reason: Gate G1 (issue #139, tracked in #138): repin's completeness claim is now computed, not asserted -- "complete" cannot be reported without stating the scope it covers. #133 showed why: repin --write printed clean/filesChanged 0 while digests it never scanned were stale, and nothing in the report said what had (or had not) actually been looked at. `scanCoverage` makes that scope explicit (artifact types consumed, paths scanned, excluded prefixes) instead of the bare `clean` boolean alone.
